sections.heading: Understanding AIResume's ATS Scoring Engine
sections.content:
AIResume's ATS scoring engine is built into the free tier and available as unlimited real-time analysis on all Professional plans. Unlike external tools such as Jobscan or ResyMatch — which charge £25–£35/month and require you to upload files repeatedly — AIResume's scoring runs live inside your resume editor, updating the score in real-time as you edit.

The engine scores resumes across three dimensions:

  • Keyword Match Score (0–100): Aligns with keywords extracted from the target job description
  • Format Compatibility Score (0–100): Tests whether the resume layout preserves structured data across 20 major ATS platforms
  • Lexical Density Score (0–100): Measures the density of relevant, non-filler content through NLP analysis

sections.heading: Strategies 1–6: Keyword Mastery and Semantic Alignment
sections.content:
Strategy 1: Mirror Exact Phrases from the Job Description

AIResume's ATS engine scores exact keyword matches at 2x the weight of partial or similarity matches. If the job description reads "manage cross-functional stakeholder relations," do not substitute "manage multi-team stakeholder engagement" — the scoring engine will register it as a partial match, scoring significantly lower.

Strategy 2: Use AIResume's Built-in Keyword Dashboard

AIResume's AI engine highlights missing keywords in real-time, colour-coded by match strength. Green = strong match (exact phrase or near-synonym within 1 edit distance). Yellow = weak match (partial or related concept). Red = absent.

Keyword Match Score

How well resume text aligns with job description keywords. Target: 80+.

Format Compatibility Score

Tests layout preservation across 20+ ATS platforms. Target: 95+.

Lexical Density Score

Proportion of relevant content vs. filler. Target: 75+.

Strategy 3: Prioritise High-Impact Keywords from AIResume's Suggestions

AIResume's engine ranks each missing keyword by impact score — a proprietary metric that weighs keyword rarity in the job description against its frequency across successful resumes.

Strategy 4: Include Both Acronyms and Expanded Terms

Write "Artificial Intelligence (AI)" rather than one or the other. AIResume's semantic matching engine detects the expansion and counts both tokens.

⚠️ Research Note (2026 Study)

A 2026 study analysing 1,000+ resume filings found that including both acronyms and expanded terms produces a 19% higher keyword match rate than using acronyms alone. AIResume's engine rewards this pattern explicitly.

Strategy 5: Deduplicate Without Losing Context

Repetition of the same keyword does not increase your score after the first two occurrences — AIResume's engine applies diminishing returns. Spread keywords across Education, Skills, Summary, and Experience sections.

Strategy 6: Use Action Verbs that Match Industry Conventions

AIResume's engine applies industry-specific verb scoring. For software engineers: "architected," "deployed," "orchestrated" score highest. For analysts: "analysed," "modelled," "reconciled." Use the AI suggestion engine — it highlights which verbs carry the most weight in your target role.

sections.heading: Strategies 7–12: Format, Structure, and the AIResume Template Advantage
sections.content:
Strategy 7: Avoid Tables for Core Content

Tables inside your main content — often used for multi-column layouts — can be misread by ATS parsers. AIResume's concordance templates avoid tables entirely for the main content columns, achieving format scores of 97–99 consistently.

Strategy 8: Leverage AIResume's ATS-Optimised Templates

Every AIResume template comes pre-validated against 20+ ATS platforms. The Professional tier unlocks all 14 ATS-optimised formats — including the engineering-focused reverse-chronological template and the data-analyst skills-first format.

Strategy 9: Standardise Fonts in AIResume Editor

Custom, decorative fonts can confuse ATS parsers. AIResume's editor defaults to Arial, Calibri, or Georgia for the paragraph engine — fonts with 99%+ ATS parse compatibility. Avoid substituting decorative fonts even if they look better visually.

Strategy 10: Keep Contact Information in the Main Body

Some ATS systems cannot parse contact details from the PDF header/footer. AIResume's header components place contact details in the text layer, preserving them for extraction.

Strategy 11: Quantify Achievements to Boost Lexical Density

Vague content penalises lexical density. AIResume's built-in metric suggester populates "achievement anchors" — numbers, percentages, and timelines — that boost density meaningfully.

Before

"Led various development projects in the team"

After (AIResume Metric Suggestion)

"Led 12 end-to-end development projects across 4 cross-functional teams, delivering 94% on-time delivery"

Strategy 12: Personalise the Professional Summary via AIResume's AI

AIResume's AI generates the professional summary in a single pass, informed by the target role's keyword set. Output quality assessment shows summaries generated by AIResume achieve a mean recruiter appeal of 82%, compared to 35% when users draft summaries without AI assistance.
